source_refs.note: Topic 31.2.2 (PDF 222). The book's statement that microplastics are 'found to be carcinogenic' in humans is reported with a warning that this has not been established; flagged for review.

blocks.text: Many toxic materials are entering the environment; plastics and heavy metals are two major concerns. They are widely used because of their useful properties, but their long-term effects can be lethal.
Heavy metals: lead (Pb), mercury (Hg) and cadmium (Cd) are common in electronics, batteries and fluorescent lights. They can get into groundwater, from where they pass into living organisms.

Plastics: many plastics contain toxic additives such as phthalates or bisphenol A (BPA), which can interfere with hormones. Microplastics are now found in oceans, soil and even food, and have long-term effects on human life and ecosystems. In humans, microplastics are suspected to be carcinogenic (cancer-causing).
